svg.title: init always delivers the framework through a review you can see — init routes through a review from any branch, and steps aside only when you opt out
svg.text: init always delivers the framework through a review you
Scenario: init routes through a review from any branch, and steps aside only when you opt out
you started on an experiment branch
the opt-out you ask for on purpose

g.text: Given a developer has cloned a project that already has a main branch
The cloned copy of a project that already has main: git shows main as the current branch
before the installer runs.
When the installer finishes setup on the project that already had main
The installer finishes on the existing main; the finished screen still names the
init-framework-devsecops merge request — the page where changes get reviewed before joining
main. The test also checks the install log.
Then init has opened the merge request into the main that already
existed
The merge request init opened from init-framework-devsecops into the main that was already
there. The test also checks through the API that it is open.
And GitLab lists main next to the init-framework-devsecops branch
The branches page: the main that was already there, and the framework branch init made from
it. The test also checks both branches through the API.
Given a developer is working on an experiment branch instead of main
The cloned copy switched to a throwaway experiment branch named spike/poc: git shows it as
current, main still there, before the installer runs.
When the installer finishes setup while on the experiment branch
The installer finishes while the developer is still on spike/poc; the finished screen still
names the merge request — the page where changes get reviewed before joining main. The test
also checks the install log.
Then init started the framework branch from main, not from the
experiment branch
The merge request aims at main, and its branch started from main, never from spike/poc. The
test also checks through the API that it is open into main.
And GitLab shows only main and the framework branch, never the local
experiment branch
The branches page holds main and init-framework-devsecops only; the local spike/poc was
never pushed. The test also checks all three through the API.
Given a developer has set the installer to deliver straight to main
The freshly cloned blank project, installer set to direct-delivery mode — git shows no
commits yet before it runs.
When the installer finishes setup in direct-delivery mode
The installer finishes in direct-delivery mode; it names no merge request — the changes go
straight to main with no review step. The test also checks the finished line in the install
log.
Then init has sent the starter README to main with no merge request
The branches page shows main alone: no init-framework-devsecops branch, and no merge request
was opened. The test also checks all three through the API.
And the project's main holds only the starter README
The project home page: main holds just the starter README; the framework stays in the local
copy on disk. The test also checks through the API that main exists.
